title: Sources of sodium in US adults from 3 geographic regions
authors: Harnack LJ, Cogswell ME, Shikany JM, Gardner CD, Gillespie C, Loria CM, et al.
population: Adults in Birmingham AL, Palo Alto CA and Minneapolis-St. Paul MN, with equal numbers of women and men from black, Asian, Hispanic and non-Hispanic white groups; four record-assisted 24-hour dietary recalls with duplicate samples of salt added at home
funder: Funding was provided through a research contract (Broad Agency Announcement) with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (contract 200-2012M-52155).
result: Sodium added to food outside the home supplied 70.9% of sodium intake (66.3% to 75.0% across subgroups), sodium inherent to food 14.2%, salt added in home food preparation 5.6% and salt added at the table 4.9%; tap water, supplements and antacids each under 0.5%.
